transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I start out really motivated, but I keep zoning out when people explain what to do and end up not finishing my class assignments or business tasks the way they were asked. It's just making things really difficult right now with my college classes and trying to run my online shop.
Have you struggled with these difficulties in staying focused and finishing tasks since you were a child, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

It's gotten much worse over the last two years with my college classes, but I've actually struggled with this since I was a kid. Back in elementary school, my teachers always complained about me getting out of my seat and rushing through projects, and my parents used to joke that I was like a wind-up toy that never stopped.
Besides the trouble with focus, have you been feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or unusually anxious and worried about most things in your daily life over these past two years?

No, I don't really feel persistently sad or anxious about everyday things. I definitely get stressed and frustrated when I fall behind on my schoolwork or business, but it's not a constant feeling of sadness or general worry.
Do you still find yourself frequently fidgeting, having trouble sitting still for long periods, or acting impulsively without thinking through the consequences?

Yes, definitely—I'm constantly jiggling my leg or tapping my fingers, and holding still feels so uncomfortable, like I have energy crawling under my skin. I'm always popping up from my seat during class, and I get so impatient that I constantly blurt out answers, finish people's sentences, or get super antsy waiting in lines. It just feels like this constant restless pressure inside me that I can't turn off.
